subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: What should the WebChat `chat.send` success contract be when Codex native-thread preflight or startup cannot prove a turn can begin?
rationale: Changing this boundary can affect public non-blocking ACK semantics, latency, duplicate handling, transcript persistence, and native-thread recovery policy, so automation should not choose it without maintainer intent.

options.title: ACK then bounded visible recovery
options.body: Keep the non-blocking ACK, but require a timeout-backed post-ACK path that either reaches agent-run start, force-rotates safely, or emits a visible terminal failure and health/audit signal.

options.title: Fail before ACK on unsafe Codex state
options.body: Delay or reject `chat.send` until Codex preflight proves the native thread is runnable, trading latency and contract change for stronger send semantics.

options.title: Codex-only force rotation
options.body: On oversized or orphaned native-thread evidence, clear the binding and seed a fresh thread before dispatch while leaving the broader WebChat ACK contract unchanged.

recommendation.title: ACK then bounded visible recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the non-blocking ACK, but require a timeout-backed post-ACK path that either reaches agent-run start, force-rotates safely, or emits a visible terminal failure and health/audit signal.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the latest merged native overflow rotation work that would most directly constrain the Codex side of this decision.
